The catalogue Codex reads, at the one path it looks for a repository's own: `$REPO_ROOT/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. It is the Codex half of what `../../.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` is for Claude Code, and `../../.codex-plugin/plugin.json` — which describes the plugin but names no catalogue — is what it points a Codex reader at.

It is not the only thing that would work, and the measurement is worth recording rather than discovering twice: with this file moved away, `codex plugin marketplace add .` falls back to `../../.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, reads that entry's plain-string `source`, and installs the same plugin at the same version. This file is shipped anyway because that fallback is a behaviour of one vendor's parser reading another vendor's manifest, measured here and documented nowhere, while `$REPO_ROOT/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is the path Codex's own documentation names. A catalogue reached by the documented route survives a Claude Code manifest change; one reached by the fallback is a dependency on two vendors continuing to agree by accident.

`source.path` is `./`, the repository root, because that is where the plugin manifest and the `skills/` directory it points at both live — the same reason the Claude Code catalogue's source is `"./"`.

Measured with codex-cli 0.149.0, and the two halves differ from Claude Code in ways a reader should not have to discover.

Registration and enablement are per user, and a repository cannot do either on a contributor's behalf. `codex plugin marketplace add .` writes `[marketplaces.lattice]` into `~/.codex/config.toml` and `codex plugin add` writes `[plugins."lattice@lattice"] enabled = true` beside it; those two tables are what enables the plugin for every session that user starts. The same tables in this repository's own `../../.codex/config.toml` do nothing — `codex plugin marketplace list` stays empty even with the project trusted, and the project layer is demonstrably read, because a top-level `model` key in that file takes effect. Only the PERSONAL catalogue at `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is discovered with no command at all; the repository-root copy this file is never gets that treatment. There is therefore no Codex equivalent of the one-line `extraKnownMarketplaces` entry that does it for everyone in `../../.claude/settings.json` — for the plugin mechanism. The sibling `../skills` directory — a checked-in copy of the repository-root `skills/`, byte-compared by `scripts/check-skills.mjs` — is what does that job here: the Agent Skills shared project directory, read by every Codex session in this repository with no command (measured via `codex debug prompt-input`), and since this manifest declares nothing but `skills`, the copy delivers everything the plugin would. A copy rather than a symlink because a Windows checkout materializes symlinks as text files, silently. This catalogue stays for the by-name install into sessions OUTSIDE this repository; a session with both routes lists each skill twice, harmlessly.

Installation also COPIES the tree into `~/.codex/plugins/cache/lattice/lattice/<version>/` rather than following a live path — an edit to a skill reaches a Codex session only after the plugin is re-added. `../../docs/skills/installation.md` documents both as the steps they are.

The version in that cache path is read from `../../.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, which is on the version chain `../../docs/skills/versioning.md` owns; this file deliberately carries no version of its own, so there is nothing here for that chain to drift from.
